newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares hit record highs in electronic trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares hit record highs in electronic trade.

text.p: Germany's IBIS DAX index rallied to end electronic trade on Thursday at a new all-time closing high, having made a new record high at 3,739.28 points late in the day.
Dealers said that sentiment was lifted by advances on Wall Street and underpinned by the firm dollar.
The IBIS DAX index of 30 German blue-chips ended up 65.29 points, or 1.78 percent, at 3,737.16 points. The DAX index, which gauges bourse trade, ended up 0.83 percent at 3,707.99 points earlier on.
"The dollar is strong today and the retail figures in the U.S. were encouraging," a German share trader said.
Also supportive were U.S. retail sales, which dropped 0.1 percent in May to a seasonally adjusted $210.3 billion after revised drops of 0.9 percent in April and 0.3 percent in March.
There was still a lot of uncertainty around about monetary union, seen limiting further advances to new record highs.
Of central importance was the row between Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer over revaluation of assets.
The Bundesbank shot down an original proposal to use the revaluation proceeds to help Germany meet criteria goals in the Maastricht Treaty.
"Everyone is intrigued as to what is going to happen," one trader said. In the event the Bundesbank issued a soothing statement, which was generally viewed as low on content.
A stronger opening on Wall Street soon after the issue of the Bundesbank statement gave some inspiration, pushing the IBIS DAX index back into record territory.

Among shares on the move was Altana, which ended down 75 marks, or 4.21 percent at 1,705 marks, falling after the company said that market speculation of an imminent drugs launch in the United States was premature and that no takeover was in sight.
Among the day's biggest winners was drugs group Degussa AG, which closed up 6.79 marks or 7.75 percent, at 934.40 marks.

Dealers said they were baffled as to why the share was rising so strongly. "With a lot of these second liners you do see one or two aggressive buyers or sellers moving the market strongly," the trader said.
A company spokesman was also unaware of the reasons for the rise in the share price.
